historical_extraction_contract.output_layout: one wide parquet per module ({db}/{module}.parquet): id + time + one column per concept — NOT per-concept files. Matches the web export path (webserver/dataio.py).
historical_extraction_contract.load_call: load_concepts(module_concepts, merge=True) once per module inside keep_cache; do NOT hand-write a per-concept merge (time-column mismatch -> Cartesian blow-up -> OOM).
historical_extraction_contract.batching: adaptive and result-invariant: one-shot when memory permits; streamed exports continuously size the first batch from currently available memory after reserving 25% (at least 2 GiB), round down to 5,000 stays, and then resize later batches from measured process-tree working set, capped at 67,000. An 8 GiB-available host therefore starts at 40,000 stays. Sepsis derivation reuses the outer batch rather than imposing a hidden 2,000-stay sub-batch. Explicit batch_size remains authoritative. Both streamed and one-shot launchers use the process-effective memory envelope: Linux honours cgroup-v2 memory.max/current, while macOS and Windows use portable host-memory detection. Below 24 GiB available the profile remains 1 worker/1GB DuckDB/256MB cache; 24/32/64-GiB tiers scale to 2/4/8 workers, 2/4/8GB DuckDB and 2/6/8GB cache.
historical_extraction_contract.spill: DuckDB temp + batch spill default to <output_dir>/.easyicu_spill (the output drive), not system /tmp.
historical_extraction_contract.row_grain: demographics is exactly one row per stay using nearest-to-0h non-null static values and recomputed BMI; every other module is unique on null-equal (stay_id, charttime), with boolean any, numeric median, and conflicting-string fail-closed consolidation. Each file manifest binds the primary key audit and exact Parquet SHA-256.

historical_merge_oom_safety.method: load_concepts(merge=True) on the trickiest mixed-time-axis modules (respiratory: vent_start/vent_end intervals + charttime points; medications rate concepts; circulatory) at 150 patients per DB.
historical_merge_oom_safety.conclusion: 19-153 rows/patient = normal ICU time-series density, no Cartesian explosion on any of the 6 databases. Cartesian blow-up is a per-patient property, so this generalises to full cohort scale. merge=True normalises the time axis before joining; the previous OOM came from a hand-written merge on inconsistent time columns (now removed).
